claim: For unrestricted complex five-mode Fourier polynomials \(P(z,w)=a+bz+cz^{-1}+dw+ew^{-1}\) on the probability-normalized two-torus, the sharp inequality is \(\int |P|^4 \,dm\le (27/11)(|a|^2+|b|^2+|c|^2+|d|^2+|e|^2)^2\). Nonzero equality occurs exactly for \((a,b,c,d,e)=\lambda(\sqrt3,\sqrt2e^{i\theta},\sqrt2e^{-i\theta},\sqrt2e^{i\phi},\sqrt2e^{-i\phi})\). An exact global nonnegative stability identity for normalized coefficients resolves the deficit into shell imbalance, axis imbalance, opposite-arm imbalance, and phase deficit, as specified in RESULT.md. The complete theorem holds also on product cyclic tori with orders at least five.
integrity: The derivation uses exact autocorrelation Fourier orthogonality, elementary AM-GM, explicit completed squares, and exact equality conditions; no numerical assertions serve as universal proof. No independent audit or validation has been conducted.
scientific_limitations: The theorem covers the five-frequency planar nearest-neighbor cross and nonaliasing finite grids N,M>=5 at the fourth moment, not general Lee crosses, small grids or sharp distance-to-orbit stability metrics. Finite checker tests corroborate, but do not constitute proof. Earlier unindexed equivalent formulations may exist.
title: Sharp fourth-moment rigidity and an exact defect identity for the five-point planar Fourier cross
